fasti.note: Gaius Caesar, Augustus' adopted son, consul in the East; meets Phraates V on the Euphrates (AD 2).
Lucius Caesar dies at Massilia (20 August). Tiberius returns from Rhodes.
Augustus' powers renewed for ten years.
Gaius Caesar dies in Lycia (21 February). Augustus adopts Tiberius (26 June), who adopts Germanicus. Lex Aelia Sentia regulates manumission.
Lex Valeria Cornelia: destinatio centuries of senators and equites pre-select candidates (Tabula Hebana). Tiberius reaches the Elbe.

Aerarium militare founded, funded by a 5% inheritance tax (vicesima hereditatium) and 1% sales tax. Vigiles created. Judaea annexed; census of Quirinius. Great Pannonian and Dalmatian revolt (6-9) cancels the campaign against Maroboduus.
Agrippa Postumus banished to Planasia. Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.
Ovid relegated to Tomis. Julia the Younger exiled. Pannonian rebels surrender at the Bathinus.

Lex Papia Poppaea, carried by two unmarried suffects, revises the marriage laws. Dalmatian revolt ends. Varus and three legions (XVII, XVIII, XIX) destroyed in the Teutoburg Forest (September) by Arminius.
Temple of Concord rededicated by Tiberius (16 January).
Ban on astrologers' consultations about death.
Gaius (Caligula) born at Antium (31 August). Tiberius' Pannonian triumph (23 October).

Augustus' powers and Tiberius' tribunicia potestas renewed; Tiberius given imperium equal to Augustus' in the provinces. Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.

Census of 4,937,000 citizens (Res Gestae 8). Death of Augustus at Nola (19 August); accession of Tiberius. Agrippa Postumus killed. Mutinies of the Pannonian and Rhine legions. Elections transferred from the people to the Senate (Tacitus, Ann. 1.15).
Germanicus visits the Teutoburg battlefield; recovers the eagle of XIX.
Germanicus defeats Arminius at Idistaviso and the Angrivarian Wall; fleet wrecked in the North Sea. Trial and suicide of Marcus Scribonius Libo Drusus, brother of the consul.

Germanicus' triumph (26 May). Cappadocia and Commagene annexed. Earthquake destroys twelve cities of Asia, including Sardis; tax remission. Revolt of Tacfarinas in Africa (17-24). Deaths of Livy and Ovid (17 or 18). Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.

Germanicus in the East crowns Artaxias in Armenia; visits Egypt without permission (19). Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.

Death of Germanicus at Antioch (10 October), suspected poisoning by Gnaeus Piso. Expulsion of Jews and Isis worshippers from Rome. Lex Iunia Norbana on informally freed slaves (Junian Latins) perhaps of this year. Arminius murdered. Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.

Trial and suicide of Gnaeus Calpurnius Piso; senatus consultum de Cn. Pisone patre (bronze copies from Baetica, published 1996). Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.
Revolt of Florus and Sacrovir in Gaul. Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.
Drusus receives tribunicia potestas. Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.

Death of Drusus (14 September), later said to be poisoned by Sejanus and Livilla. Praetorians concentrated in the Castra Praetoria. Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.
Tacfarinas killed. Slave rising in Apulia. Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.

Prosecution and suicide of the historian Cremutius Cordus; his books burned. Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.

Tiberius withdraws from Rome to Campania, then Capri (27). Pontius Pilate prefect of Judaea (26-36). Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.

Collapse of the amphitheatre at Fidenae: 50,000 killed or injured (Tacitus, Ann. 4.62). Fire on the Caelian. Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.
Revolt of the Frisii over the ox-hide tribute. Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.

The 'two Gemini', the consular date given by Tertullian and others for the crucifixion (modern estimates prefer 30 or 33). Death of Livia. Agrippina the Elder and Nero Caesar banished. Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.

Velleius Paterculus' history dedicated to Vinicius. Drusus Caesar imprisoned. Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.
Sejanus consul with Tiberius; arrested on a letter read to the Senate by the suffect Regulus (18 October) and executed with his children. Macro becomes praetorian prefect.
Purge of Sejanus' associates. Domitius, father of Nero.

Credit crisis: enforcement of Caesar's law on investment in Italian land triggers a liquidity crunch; Tiberius lends 100 million sesterces interest-free for three years (Tacitus, Ann. 6.16-17). Deaths of Agrippina the Elder and Drusus Caesar. Galba is the future emperor. Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.

Phoenix reported in Egypt. Lucius Vitellius (father of the emperor) later governs Syria. Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.
Servilius Nonianus, historian. Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.

Fire on the Aventine. Vitellius deposes Pilate. Armenian and Parthian settlement. Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.
Tiberius dies at Misenum (16 March); Gaius (Caligula) accedes and holds his first consulship from 1 July with his uncle Claudius. Nero born at Antium (15 December).

Drusilla deified. Anti-Jewish riots in Alexandria; Flaccus prefect. Macro forced to suicide. Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.
Bridge of boats from Baiae to Puteoli. Conspiracy of Gaetulicus and Lepidus; Agrippina the Younger and Julia Livilla exiled. Gaius to the Rhine.

Gaius sole consul at the start of the year. Abortive British expedition (the sea-shells). Ptolemy of Mauretania executed; revolt of Aedemon. Philo's embassy to Gaius; order to erect his statue in the Jerusalem temple. Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.

Gaius murdered in the Palatine (24 January) by praetorian tribunes Cassius Chaerea and Cornelius Sabinus; the Senate debates restoring the Republic while the praetorians proclaim Claudius. Seneca exiled to Corsica. Claudius' letter to the Alexandrians.

Revolt of Furius Camillus Scribonianus in Dalmatia collapses in five days. Mauretania divided into two provinces. Harbour at Ostia (Portus) begun. Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.

Invasion of Britain under Aulus Plautius (four legions, c. 40,000 men); Claudius present at the fall of Camulodunum. Lycia annexed. Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.

Claudius' British triumph. Death of Herod Agrippa I; Judaea again under procurators. Achaea and Macedonia returned to the Senate. Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.

Solar eclipse on Claudius' birthday (1 August) announced in advance by edict. Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.

Thrace annexed. Edict of Claudius on the citizenship of the Anauni (Tabula Clesiana). Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.

Ludi Saeculares for Rome's 800th year. Claudius and Vitellius as censors (47-48). Valerius Asiaticus forced to suicide. Corbulo halts beyond the Rhine on orders. Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.

Claudius' speech on admitting Gallic nobles to the Senate (Lyon tablet, CIL XIII 1668; Tacitus, Ann. 11.24). Messalina's 'marriage' to Silius; her execution. Census of 5,984,072 citizens (Tacitus). Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.

Claudius marries his niece Agrippina (senatus consultum permits uncle-niece marriage). Seneca recalled as Nero's tutor. Pomerium extended (49). Jews expelled from Rome 'impulsore Chresto' (Suetonius, Claudius 25.4; date from Orosius). Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.

Claudius adopts Nero (25 February). Colonia Claudia Ara Agrippinensium (Cologne). Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.
Caratacus captured and displayed in Rome. Burrus praetorian prefect. Nero assumes the toga virilis early. Vespasian suffect consul for the last two months.

Fucine Lake drainage tunnel opened with a naumachia; Aqua Claudia and Anio Novus completed (52). Senatus consultum Claudianum on free women cohabiting with slaves. Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.

Nero marries Octavia. Procurators given jurisdiction in fiscal cases. Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.

Claudius dies (13 October), allegedly poisoned with mushrooms by Agrippina; Nero accedes aged 16. Seneca's Apocolocyntosis. Parthians install Tiridates in Armenia. Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.

Britannicus poisoned at dinner (February). Corbulo given the Armenian command. Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.
Seneca suffect consul. Debate on re-enslaving ungrateful freedmen.
Wooden amphitheatre of Nero in the Campus Martius. Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.

Corbulo takes Artaxata. Nero proposes abolishing indirect taxes; instead tax contracts published (Tacitus, Ann. 13.50-51). Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.

Agrippina murdered at Baiae (March) after the collapsing-boat attempt. Riot in the Pompeii amphitheatre; games banned there for ten years. Juvenalia. Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.

Neronia, quinquennial Greek-style games. Corbulo installs Tigranes VI in Armenia; Suetonius Paulinus attacks Mona (60 or 61). Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.

Revolt of Boudica (60 or 61): Camulodunum, Londinium and Verulamium sacked; 70,000-80,000 killed (Tacitus); defeated by Suetonius Paulinus. Murder of the urban prefect Pedanius Secundus by a slave; all 400 of his household executed.

Death of Burrus; Tigellinus prefect; Seneca retires. Octavia divorced and killed; Nero marries Poppaea. Paetus surrenders at Rhandeia. Earthquake at Pompeii (5 February 62 or 63). Maiestas trials revived. Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.

Corbulo's settlement at Rhandeia: Tiridates to receive the Armenian crown from Nero. Pontus annexed (64/65). Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.

Great Fire of Rome (from 19 July, six days plus a second outbreak); 3 of 14 regions destroyed, 7 badly damaged. Christians punished as scapegoats (Tacitus, Ann. 15.44). Domus Aurea begun. Denarius reduced (c. 3.4 g, silver lowered to c. 93%) and aureus lightened. Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.

Pisonian conspiracy (April): suicides of Seneca, Lucan, Piso and the consul Vestinus. Death of Poppaea. Petronius forced to suicide (66). Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.

Tiridates crowned in Rome; temple of Janus closed. Nero's tour of Greece (66-67). Jewish revolt; Cestius Gallus defeated at Beth Horon. Thrasea Paetus forced to suicide. Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.

Nero proclaims the freedom of Achaea at Corinth (28 November); begins the Corinth canal. Corbulo summoned and ordered to kill himself. Vespasian conquers Galilee; Josephus captured at Jotapata. Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.

Revolt of Vindex in Gaul (March), crushed by Verginius Rufus at Vesontio; Galba proclaimed in Spain. Nero declared a public enemy, commits suicide (9 June). Galba accedes. Silius Italicus the epic poet.

Year of the Four Emperors. Galba and Vinius killed (15 January); Otho; First Battle of Bedriacum (14 April) and Otho's suicide; Vitellius; Vespasian proclaimed at Alexandria (1 July); Second Bedriacum (24-25 October) and sack of Cremona; Capitol burned (19 December); Vitellius killed (20 December). Revolt of Civilis on the Rhine. Many further suffects appointed by successive emperors.

Lex de imperio Vespasiani (bronze tablet, CIL VI 930) probably of December 69. Titus destroys Jerusalem and the Temple (August-September). Civilis and the Imperium Galliarum suppressed by Petillius Cerialis. Capitol rebuilding begun.
Joint triumph of Vespasian and Titus over Judaea (June). Temple of Janus closed. Fiscus Iudaicus: the temple tax diverted to Jupiter Capitolinus.
Commagene annexed. Temple of Peace begun (dedicated 75).

Vespasian and Titus censors (73-74); adlection of new senators from Italy and the provinces. Fall of Masada (73 or 74). Philosophers expelled. Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.

Latin rights granted to all of Spain (announced 73/74; Pliny NH 3.30), leading to the Flavian municipal charters (Irni, Malaca, Salpensa). Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.
Temple of Peace dedicated. Alans raid Media and Armenia. Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.
Hadrian born (24 January) in Rome or Italica. Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.

Pliny the Elder dedicates the Natural History to Titus. Agricola suffect consul (77 or 76) and governor of Britain from 77 or 78. Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.
Agricola campaigns in North Wales and Anglesey (77/78). Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.

Vespasian dies at Aquae Cutiliae (23 June): 'vae, puto deus fio'. Titus accedes. Eruption of Vesuvius (24 August by the manuscript tradition of Pliny's letter; October argued from finds) buries Pompeii, Herculaneum, Stabiae; Pliny the Elder dies.

Fire in Rome destroys the Capitol again, the Pantheon and the Saepta. Plague. Flavian Amphitheatre (Colosseum) inaugurated with 100 days of games. Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.
Flavius Silva, the conqueror of Masada. Titus dies (13 September); Domitian accedes. Arch of Titus erected after his death.

Silver content of the denarius raised to Augustan standard (82-85), then reduced again in 85. Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.

Domitian's war against the Chatti; Taunus limes. Agricola's victory at Mons Graupius (83 or 84). Domitian takes the title Germanicus. Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.

Agricola recalled. Domitian raises legionary pay by a third (from 225 to 300 denarii per year). Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.

Domitian censor perpetuus. Dacians under Diurpaneus (or Decebalus) invade Moesia, killing the governor Oppius Sabinus. Moesia later split (86). Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.

Cornelius Fuscus, praetorian prefect, killed in Dacia. Capitoline Games founded. Antoninus Pius born (19 September). Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.

Inchtuthil legionary fortress abandoned unfinished (c. 86-87) as troops are withdrawn from Britain for the Danube. Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.

Ludi Saeculares (Domitian's computation; Tacitus as quindecimvir). Tettius Julianus defeats the Dacians at Tapae. Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.
Revolt of Antonius Saturninus at Mogontiacum (1 January) suppressed by Lappius Maximus. Peace with Decebalus, who receives subsidies and engineers. Expulsion of philosophers.
Upper and Lower Germany formally constituted as provinces (by 90). Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.
Trajan consul ordinarius. Vestal Cornelia buried alive. Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.

Sarmatian war; a legion (XXI Rapax?) lost. Edict restricting vine planting in the provinces (Suetonius, Dom. 7). Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.

Death of Agricola (23 August). Treason trials of the Stoic opposition: Herennius Senecio, Arulenus Rusticus, Helvidius Priscus the Younger executed. Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.
Epictetus among philosophers expelled from Rome (c. 93-95). Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.

Clemens, Domitian's cousin, executed after his consulship for 'atheism'; his wife Flavia Domitilla exiled. Acilius Glabrio (cos. 91) executed. Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.
Domitian murdered (18 September) in a palace conspiracy; damnatio memoriae. Nerva proclaimed by the Senate.

Verginius Rufus died after breaking his hip; Tacitus as suffect gave his funeral oration. Praetorian mutiny under Casperius Aelianus; Nerva adopts Trajan (October). Alimenta instituted under Nerva (or Trajan).
Nerva dies (27/28 January); Trajan accedes at Cologne and stays on the Rhine and Danube until 99. Tacitus' Agricola and Germania. Frontinus, curator aquarum, writes De aquis.
Trajan enters Rome on foot. Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.
Pliny the Younger, suffect in September-October, delivers the Panegyricus. Thamugadi (Timgad) founded. Trial of Marius Priscus for extortion in Africa.

First Dacian War (101-102); battle at Tapae. Danube canal at the Iron Gates (inscription of 101). Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.
Decebalus submits; Trajan takes the title Dacicus. Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.

Apollodorus of Damascus builds the Danube bridge at Drobeta (103-105). Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.

Fire damages the Domus Aurea; Baths of Trajan built over it (dedicated 109). Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.
Second Dacian War begins. Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.

Sarmizegetusa taken; Decebalus' suicide; Dacia annexed; Decebalus' treasure (said by Lydus, from Crito, to be 5 million pounds of gold) funds Trajan's building. Nabataean kingdom annexed as Arabia (22 March epoch of Bostra).

Trajan's Dacian triumph: 123 days of games, 11,000 animals, 10,000 gladiators (Dio 68.15). Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.
Hadrian suffect consul (May).
Baths of Trajan and the Aqua Traiana dedicated. Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.

Pliny the Younger legatus in Bithynia-Pontus (c. 110-112); correspondence with Trajan, including the letter on Christians (Ep. 10.96-97). Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.
Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.
Forum of Trajan and Basilica Ulpia dedicated (1 January). Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.

Trajan's Column dedicated (12 May). Trajan leaves for the East (October). Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.
Armenia annexed. Trajan voted the title Optimus. Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.

Pedo killed in the Antioch earthquake (13 December 115), which Trajan narrowly survived. Mesopotamia overrun. Jewish diaspora revolt (115-117) in Cyrene, Egypt and Cyprus. Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.

Ctesiphon taken; Trajan reaches the Persian Gulf; Parthicus. Revolts in the new provinces; Hatra resists. Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.
Trajan dies at Selinus in Cilicia (8 August); Hadrian announces his adoption, disputed then and since; abandons Mesopotamia and Assyria.

Execution of four consulars (Palma, Celsus, Nigrinus, Quietus). Debt remission: 900 million sesterces of arrears burned in Trajan's Forum. Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.
Hadrian's last consulship. Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.

Titus Aurelius Fulvus Boionius Arrius Antoninus
fasti.note: The future Antoninus Pius consul ordinarius. Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.

Marcus Aurelius born (26 April). Hadrian begins his first great tour (121-125). Temple of Venus and Roma begun (21 April). Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.

Hadrian in Britain; Hadrian's Wall begun under Aulus Platorius Nepos. Suetonius dismissed as ab epistulis. Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.
Hadrian averts a Parthian war by meeting Osroes on the Euphrates. Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.
Hadrian in Greece; initiated at Eleusis. Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.

consuls: Marcus Lollius Paullinus Decimus Valerius Asiaticus Saturninus
fasti.note: Hadrian returns to Rome via Athens. Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.
Pantheon rebuilt (c. 118-126/128), retaining Agrippa's dedication. Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.

Italy divided among four consular iuridici (or under Hadrian generally). Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.

Hadrian in Africa: address to the army at Lambaesis (1 July, CIL VIII 18042). Accepts the title pater patriae. Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.

Celsus the jurist; senatus consultum Iuventianum on inheritance claims. Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.

Antinous drowns in the Nile (October); Antinoopolis founded. Aelia Capitolina planned at Jerusalem. Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.

Edictum perpetuum codified by Salvius Julianus (c. 130-131). Panhellenion inaugurated (131/132). Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.
Bar Kokhba revolt in Judaea (132-135/136). Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.
Sextus Julius Severus transferred from Britain to Judaea. Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.
Arrian, governor of Cappadocia, repels the Alans (134/135). Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.

Fall of Betar; Judaea renamed Syria Palaestina; Jews barred from Aelia Capitolina. Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.

Hadrian adopts Ceionius Commodus as Lucius Aelius Caesar. Servianus (aged 90) and his grandson Pedanius Fuscus forced to die. Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.
Lucius Aelius dies 1 January 138. Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.
Hadrian adopts Antoninus (25 February), who adopts Marcus Aurelius and Lucius Verus. Hadrian dies at Baiae (10 July).

Antoninus accepts pater patriae. Mausoleum of Hadrian completed. Sothic cycle begins (Censorinus). Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.

Death of Faustina the Elder (October/November 140 or 141), deified; puellae Faustinianae. Antonine Wall begun (142). Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.
Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.

Lollius Urbicus in Britain; Antonine Wall built between Forth and Clyde. Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.
Herodes Atticus, the Athenian magnate, consul ordinarius; his tutee Marcus' correspondence with Fronto, suffect in July-August.
Aelius Aristides' Roman Oration (143 or 155). Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.

Marcus marries Faustina the Younger. Temple of Divus Hadrianus dedicated. Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.
Septimius Severus born at Lepcis Magna (11 April 145 or 146). Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.
Marcus receives tribunicia potestas. Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.
Rome's 900th anniversary games. The ordinarius is often identified with the jurist Julianus, though the identification has been questioned.
Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.

Ptolemy's Almagest and Geography (c. 150). Justin Martyr's First Apology (c. 150-155). Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.

Antoninus Pius dies at Lorium (7 March); Marcus accedes and makes Lucius (Verus) co-Augustus, the first joint rule. Commodus born (31 August). Parthian invasion of Armenia; Severianus' legion destroyed at Elegeia.

Rusticus, Marcus' Stoic teacher, later urban prefect who tried Justin Martyr (c. 165). Verus to the East. Suffect consuls are listed only where securely attested; most imperial years had two to four further suffect pairs not listed here.

consuls: Aulus Junius Pastor Lucius Caesennius Sospes
fasti.note: Statius Priscus takes Artaxata.
Verus marries Lucilla at Ephesus.
Avidius Cassius sacks Seleucia and Ctesiphon; the 'Antonine plague' (probably smallpox) breaks out in the army and spreads west (165-166 onwards). Death of Peregrinus at Olympia.
Verus' Parthian triumph. Langobardi and Obii cross the Danube (166/167). Embassy from 'Andun' (Antoninus) reaches China per the Hou Hanshu.
Marcomannic Wars begin (167 or 168). Gold mines of Dacia attacked.
Marcus and Verus at Aquileia; plague in the army.

Lucius Verus dies at Altinum (January/February). Auction of palace treasures to fund the war. Marcomanni and Quadi invade Italy and besiege Aquileia (170 by the usual chronology), the first invasion of Italy since the Cimbri.
Costoboci raid Greece as far as Eleusis (170 or 171).
Only the cognomina are securely known for this pair in dating formulae; fuller names omitted. 'Rain miracle' against the Quadi (172 or 174) depicted on the Column of Marcus Aurelius.
Pompeianus, Syrian-born marshal and second husband of Lucilla.
Marcus writes the Meditations on campaign (c. 170-180).
Revolt of Avidius Cassius in Syria and Egypt after a false report of Marcus' death; killed after three months. Death of Faustina at Halala. Pertinax suffect consul (c. 175).
Marcus founds chairs of philosophy at Athens. Joint triumph with Commodus (23 December).
Commodus made Augustus. Martyrs of Lyon and Vienne (Eusebius, HE 5.1). SC de pretiis gladiatorum minuendis (Italica and Sardis copies, 177).
Constitutio Orfitianum on mothers' succession dated by this Orfitus (SC Orfitianum, 178). Marcus and Commodus return to the Danube.
Laugaricio inscription (Trenčín, Slovakia) of Legio II Adiutrix, 179.

consuls: Lucius Fulvius Rusticus Gaius Bruttius Praesens
fasti.note: Marcus dies at Vindobona or Sirmium (17 March); Commodus makes peace on the Danube. Martyrs of Scillium (17 July), the earliest Latin Christian document.
Conspiracy of Lucilla and Quadratus.
Perennis praetorian prefect dominates (182-185). Victories in Britain (Ulpius Marcellus, 184).
Fuller names uncertain. Perennis lynched at the demand of a deputation of 1,500 soldiers from Britain; Cleander rises. 'Deserters' war' of Maternus in Gaul (186/187).
Fuller names uncertain (Seius Fuscianus, Marcus Servilius Silanus).
Cleander sells 25 consulships for 190 (Dio 73.12).
Grain riot leads to the fall and execution of Cleander. Twenty-five suffect consuls in one year (Dio).
Fire destroys the Temple of Peace with Galen's books (191 or 192).
Commodus renames Rome Colonia Commodiana and the months after his titles; fights as a gladiator. Strangled by the athlete Narcissus (31 December).

Year of the Five Emperors: Pertinax (killed 28 March), Didius Julianus buys the throne at auction (killed 1 June), Septimius Severus proclaimed at Carnuntum (9 April); Pescennius Niger in Syria, Clodius Albinus in Britain (made Caesar). Severus replaces the praetorians with legionaries.
Niger defeated at Cyzicus, Nicaea and Issus; killed. Syria divided into Coele and Phoenice.
Severus' first Parthian war; province of Osrhoene/Mesopotamia. Severus declares himself son of Marcus Aurelius and renames his son Antoninus (Caracalla).
Byzantium falls after a three-year siege. Albinus proclaims himself Augustus. Caracalla made Caesar.

Battle of Lugdunum (19 February): Albinus defeated and killed; Lugdunum sacked; 29 senators executed. Second Parthian war: Ctesiphon sacked (late 197 or January 198). Legionaries permitted to marry (soon after).
Caracalla made Augustus (28 January), Geta Caesar. Mesopotamia a province with two legions (I and III Parthica). Hatra besieged twice in vain (198-199).
Severus in Egypt (199-200); Alexandria given a council.
Tertullian writing at Carthage. Legionary pay raised by Severus (from 300 to perhaps 400-450 denarii).
